module.title: System Design Fundamentals
module.description: Learn how large-scale applications are designed, scaled, optimized, and structured in real-world production engineering.

lessons.title: What Is System Design?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: System design is the process of planning how large applications should work, scale, communicate, and handle real-world traffic.

sections.heading: Coding Alone Is Not Enough
sections.content: Small projects work with simple code, but large applications require infrastructure planning and architecture decisions.

sections.heading: Applications Become Systems
sections.content: Modern apps contain frontend servers, APIs, databases, caching systems, authentication services, realtime systems, and cloud infrastructure.

sections.heading: System Design Focuses On Scale
sections.content: System design solves problems related to traffic, reliability, speed, maintainability, and scalability.

sections.heading: Professional Engineering Thinking
sections.content: Senior engineers think about complete ecosystems instead of isolated code files.

easyExample.title: City Planning Example
easyExample.content: Building one house is simple, but designing an entire city requires roads, electricity, traffic systems, water systems, and planning.

summary: System design focuses on scalable systems
Modern systems contain many interconnected services

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Scalability means handling increasing numbers of users, requests, and data efficiently.

sections.heading: Why Scalability Matters
sections.content: Applications that work for 100 users may completely fail for 1 million users.

sections.heading: Traffic Growth Creates Problems
sections.content: More users increase server load, database requests, API traffic, and infrastructure pressure.

sections.heading: Scalable Systems Handle Growth
sections.content: Professional applications are designed to support increasing traffic smoothly.

sections.heading: Scalability Is Core Engineering
sections.content: Large companies prioritize scalability from the beginning.

easyExample.title: Restaurant Scaling Example
easyExample.content: A small restaurant can handle 20 customers easily, but thousands of customers require larger kitchens, staff, and infrastructure.

lessons.title: Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Vertical scaling increases server power while horizontal scaling increases the number of servers.

sections.heading: Vertical Scaling
sections.content: Vertical scaling upgrades existing servers with more RAM, CPU, and storage.

sections.heading: Horizontal Scaling
sections.content: Horizontal scaling adds more servers distributing workload across systems.

sections.heading: Limitations Of Vertical Scaling
sections.content: Single servers eventually reach hardware limits.

sections.heading: Modern Systems Prefer Horizontal Scaling
sections.content: Large applications distribute traffic across many machines globally.

easyExample.title: Delivery System Example
easyExample.content: One large truck has limits, but multiple delivery vehicles can scale operations more efficiently.

summary: Modern infrastructure relies on horizontal growth

lessons.title: Load Balancers

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Load balancers distribute traffic across multiple servers to improve scalability and reliability.

sections.heading: Single Servers Become Bottlenecks
sections.content: One server cannot handle massive traffic alone reliably.

sections.heading: Traffic Distribution
sections.content: Load balancers spread requests across multiple backend servers.

sections.heading: Improved Reliability
sections.content: If one server fails, traffic moves to healthy servers automatically.

sections.heading: Core Production Infrastructure
sections.content: Almost all large-scale applications rely on load balancing.

easyExample.title: Supermarket Checkout Example
easyExample.content: Customers distribute across multiple counters instead of using one overloaded checkout line.

basicCode.title: Load Balancer Flow
basicCode.code: Users → Load Balancer → Multiple Backend Servers

summary: Large systems depend heavily on load balancing

lessons.title: Caching Systems

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Caching stores frequently used data temporarily to reduce system workload and improve speed.

sections.heading: Repeated Requests Waste Resources
sections.content: Fetching the same data repeatedly overloads databases and servers.

sections.heading: Caching Improves Performance
sections.content: Applications temporarily store commonly accessed data for faster retrieval.

sections.heading: Frontend And Backend Caching
sections.content: Modern systems use browser caches, CDN caches, API caches, and database caches.

sections.heading: Scalable Infrastructure Depends On Caching
sections.content: Large platforms heavily rely on caching to handle massive traffic.

easyExample.title: Restaurant Pre-Cooking Example
easyExample.content: Restaurants prepare common dishes in advance to serve customers faster.

summary: Large systems depend heavily on caching

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Monoliths combine everything into one application while microservices split systems into independent services.

sections.heading: Monolith Architecture
sections.content: Single applications contain frontend APIs, business logic, and infrastructure together.

sections.heading: Microservices Architecture
sections.content: Applications split authentication, payments, notifications, and APIs into separate services.

sections.heading: Advantages And Complexity
sections.content: Microservices improve scalability but significantly increase infrastructure complexity.

sections.heading: Professional Engineering Decisions
sections.content: Large companies choose architectures based on scale, teams, and operational needs.

easyExample.title: Mall vs Small Shop Example
easyExample.content: A small shop handles everything together while malls separate operations into specialized stores.
